author: potuz
content: Unfortunately, from the point of view of the protocol, the relay "is the builder". The node can't distinguish between a single endpoint serving many indices from the same builder and serving different builders. Moreover, with optimistic relaying that relay is indeed broadcasting a payload without any guarantees of it being valid. Builders that participate in such a relay with untrusted builders would be sharing the risk. And just in case this wasn't clear in my post, if builders 1 and 2 where served on endpoint X and builders 2 and 3 where served on endpoint Y, on a payload failure from 2 we'll block endpoints X **and** Y, and also mark indices 1,2 and 3 for an epoch

author: potuz
content: Builders are free to have their own unshared endpoint

author: potuz
content: And be responsible for their own actions

author: alextes

author: alextes
content: Two perhaps unforeseen consequences: i'd expect relay like entities would start managing many identities and stakes to try and stay live, effectively circumventing the intended design as it so frequently is expected to block them when they are in fact capable of correctly delivering the highest paying block. It would also result in these dead calls where some endpoints are fallbacks. The second, we'd start tracking others being blocked, and update bidding strategies accordingly, where because we know our biggest competitor can't bid, we can reduce our bids. This would hurt proposer payouts.

author: alextes
content: I also just had an idea, what about punishing either consecutive failures, 2+ in a row is ban. or % wise, where 2/32 = 0.0625 so then more than 6% failed in an epoch is ban. In both cases you only increase the number of failed / empty slots to 2 from 1 in an epoch iiuc, but on the pro builder / relay side you go from expecting this to happen some 1% of the time or multiple times a day to basically never. Unless of course an actual failure happens, in which case we want breakers to flip. Another bonus, our actual miss rate is 0.0282% it looks like so in return you could make the trigger more strict. i.e. within the last 90d we saw plenty days with 1 failure but only saw 1d with >2 misses in a single day and on that unlucky day they were still 30min+ apart. So even 2/96 failure rate, 2 in 3 epochs, which seems more strict and in expectation is a stronger breaker would effectively be much more lenient to us than what is proposed now with 1/32 being punished 😅 .

i'm conceptually quite aligned with these circuit breakers, even cutting off the full relay: it's harsh and a bit of a hair trigger, but being ignored on average for 16 slots is not really a big deal imo. i do wonder though about the builder incentives, like this encourages us to use different indices for each relay which means that a bug in a builder could potentially lead to missed slots at every relay and bring down the whole relay ecosystem.

author: mostlyblocks
content:
If there are consecutive failures, the relay is very likely at fault (more precisely, the builder is not at fault):
(1) If the failure is on the same index, the relay failed to ban a faulty builder. 
(2) if the failure is on a different index, the failure is very likely in shared infrastructure. 

Edge case is something like an AWS failure, but even then, it's likely okay to ban as continued failures are likely.
